ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is square ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the upper right, C at the lower right, and D at the lower left. Inside the square there are two semicircles: one with AB as the diameter drawn downward into the square, and the other with AD as the diameter drawn rightward into the square. The shaded part consists of two pieces: the common overlapping lens-shaped region of the two semicircles near A, and the region near C that is outside the two semicircles; the unshaded part is the region that belongs to only one of the semicircles. Reasoning: AB=2, so the side length of the square is 2, and the area is 4; the radii of the two semicircles are both 1, and the area of each semicircle is π/2. The centers of the two semicircles are respectively the midpoints of AB and AD, and the distance between the centers is √2. Their overlapping lens area is equal to the areas of two 90° sectors minus the areas of two right isosceles triangles, namely I=2(π/4-1/2)=π/2-1. The union area of the two semicircles is π-I. The area in the square outside the two semicircles is 4-(π-I). The shaded area equals the overlapping area plus the outside area: I+[4-(π-I)]=2I+4-π=2(π/2-1)+4-π=2. Therefore the area of the shaded region is 2.

raw_record.question_text: The diagram shows a square $ABCD$ and two semicircles with diameters $AB$ and $AD$. If $AB=2$, what is the area of the shaded region?

method.method_draft: First read the image: the shaded parts are the common lens of the two semicircles near A plus the region near C that lies outside both semicircles; the white parts are the portions lying in exactly one semicircle. From the text, ABCD is a square with AB=2, so each semicircle has radius 1. The semicircle centers are the midpoints of AB and AD, whose distance is sqrt(2). Their overlap lens has two 90-degree sectors minus two right isosceles triangles, so its area is 2(pi/4 - 1/2)=pi/2 - 1. Each semicircle has area pi/2, and the square has area 4. Thus shaded area = overlap + outside-union area = I + [4 - (pi - I)] with I=pi/2-1, giving 2.
